text:
Cutter Gauthier spent most of November chasing a piece of history. The goal streak that pushed him into the Rocket Richard race, as Daily Faceoff framed it, ended when Scott Wedgewood and Colorado shut out the Ducks on Nov. 19. He scored again four nights later in Seattle, and he now has 22 goals in 24 games, 12 of them in his last ten, with 17 power-play points.

The role is new. He's playing 18:49 a night, up from 17:15, and he's on the ice for 89% of Anaheim's power-play chances after 55% last season. His own chances are up too: 1.54 expected goals per 60 (the quality of his shots), from 1.36. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 99th percentile for chances from in front of the net last season.

But 22 goals on 11.6 expected is a gap that rarely holds. He's shooting 21% against 14% last season, and at five on five Anaheim gets only 44.7% of the expected goals with him on. He still ranks second of 559 skaters in wins added by his goals, behind only Tage Thompson. The shooter is real; watch where the percentage settles.
